$comment: The committed size of the code-scanning backlog, and the only thing that reads it is
the `Code scanning backlog` job in security.yml.
WHY A NUMBER AND NOT ZERO. `github/codeql-action/analyze` fails on nothing: it uploads
every alert the security-and-quality suite raises and reports success either way. So the
page has been accumulating findings that no gate has ever read, and demanding zero on the
first run would red every pull request over a backlog none of them created — the failure
mode the allocation gate exists to avoid, and the one that made the Semgrep job worthless
for months.
SO IT IS A RATCHET. The job fails when the open count exceeds `total`, which makes a new
alert a failure today. Lowering the number is the work; raising it is a decision that has
to be argued in the pull request that raises it, because nothing else here can move.
HOW TO RE-RECORD. Read the count the job prints, fix alerts until it drops, and set
`total` to what remains. Never set it to what the run reported without looking at the
difference: a count that rose because a query pack was updated is a different fact from
one that rose because somebody wrote a defect.
`bySeverity` is not enforced. It is here so a re-recording says which way the backlog
moved, rather than only that it did.
SEEDED, NOT MEASURED. The first run prints the real numbers; this file was written
before it, so `total` is null and the job reports the count and passes exactly once.
The commit that fills it in is the commit that turns this into a gate.
